verdicts.title: Recent advances on the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The log-rank conjecture is one of the fundamental open problems in communication complexity. It speculates that the deterministic communication complexity of any two-party function is equal to the log of the rank of its associated matrix, up to polynomial factors. Despite much research, we still know very little about this conjecture. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract surveys the log-rank conjecture relating deterministic communication complexity to log-rank of the associated matrix, with no mention of formal language growth complexity or any 'rank variance' quantity. It shares the communication-complexity vocabulary but does not address the specific I(G) = Θ(√RC(G)) claim.

verdicts.title: Complexity of Networks (reprise)
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
Network or graph structures are ubiquitous in the study of complex systems. Often, we are interested in complexity trends of these system as it evolves under some dynamic. An example might be looking at the complexity of a food web as species enter an ecosystem via migration or speciation, and leave via extinction.
